title: MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I DEFICIENCY, NUCLEAR TYPE 7

relationships.phenotype: MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I DEFICIENCY, NUCLEAR TYPE 7

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NDUFV2 gene (600532) on chromosome 18p11.

checks.claim: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NDUFV2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The homozygous mutation altering the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2 resulted in 70% decreased NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.
checks.explanation: The homozygous NDUFV2 mutation causes complex I deficiency. MC1DN7 is the OMIM name for this disorder.

checks.claim: The NDUFV2 gene is located on chromosome 18p11.
checks.evidence_quote: a 4-bp deletion in intron 2 (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA) of the NDUFV2 gene (encoding NADH dehydrogenase ubiquinone flavoprotein 2)
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location, but adding a gene's location is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 7 (MC1DN7) is an autosomal recessive disorder of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. It usually begins in early infancy. Reported features include hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, encephalopathy, hypotonia and lactic acidosis, and the disorder is often fatal in infancy. Mitochondrial complex I deficiency is genetically heterogeneous and can be caused by mutation in many nuclear-encoded and mitochondrial-encoded genes.

paragraphs.text: Benit et al. (2003) screened patients with complex I deficiency for mutations in nuclear-encoded complex I subunit genes. In affected sibs they identified a homozygous 4-bp deletion in intron 2 of the NDUFV2 gene. The deletion affected the splice donor site and caused skipping of exon 3.
